brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact despite Thursday volatility; CoWoS expansion easing 2027 bottleneck, HBM3E pricing firm into 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="38-8,38-10">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix shed 7–14% on July 3, 2026, in a tech selloff that spilled from Nasdaq</cite>, <cite index="43-1,43-4,43-5">but both recovered sharply July 4 with SK Hynix up 10.88% and Samsung up 8.22%</cite>. <cite index="11-6,11-16,11-17">DRAM contract prices continue to rise, driven by tight supply and manufacturers' negative production-growth expectations</cite>, with <cite index="17-2,17-7">Q2 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices forecast to rise 58–63% QoQ and NAND Flash 70–75% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="4-2,4-8">HBM3E pricing holds at ~$300/stack as of June 2026, with SK Hynix commanding 50–55% market share</cite>. <cite index="29-11">TSMC CoWoS supply–demand gap is narrowing from ~20% currently to ~10% by end-2026</cite>, with <cite index="29-2">monthly capacity reaching 120,000–140,000 wafers in 2026</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral to slight SK Hynix outperform. SK Hynix retains pole position in HBM3E with 50–55% share and locked 2026 supply. Samsung is catching up—Anthropic talks on custom chips and HBM4 qualification for Google TPU are positives—but execution risk remains. Near-term edge to SK Hনix on allocation; medium-term both benefit from memory supercycle and hyperscaler capex growth. Thursday's 14.6% drawdown in SK Hynix versus Samsung's 9.1% created tactical entry; Friday's 10.88% vs 8.22% bounce confirms defensive bid. Watch Samsung Q2 prelim (July 7) for any margin disappointment.

memory_cycle.notes: DRAM contract pricing up 93–98% in Q1 2026, decelerating to 58–63% in Q2. NAND accelerating (70–75% Q2 vs ~60% Q1). Spot pricing still rising but buyer hesitation emerging in early June. HBM crowding out commodity DRAM (3:1 wafer consumption ratio). Suppliers managing scarcity via allocation frameworks favoring hyperscalers. No meaningful capacity relief until late 2027/early 2028. Cycle peak not imminent but rate-of-change decelerating.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-2,4-8">HBM3E pricing at ~$300/stack (June 2026), HBM3 ~$200, HBM4 est. ~$500</cite>. <cite index="2-9,2-11">Supply remains constrained through 2026, lead times 20–26 weeks</cite>. <cite index="8-1,8-2">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026; HBM3E supply remains tight as vendors prioritize HBM4 ramp</cite>. <cite index="6-2,6-3">TrendForce April report: server DDR5 profitability overtook HBM in early 2026—historic first driven by DDR5 ASP escalation</cite>. <cite index="18-14">SK Hynix secured commitments covering entire 2026 HBM production in October 2025</cite>. Revenue mix tilting: <cite index="8-3">analysts forecast 2026 HBM revenue ~55% HBM4, 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 absorbing demand from Q3</cite>. <cite index="46-2">Samsung pledged 56 trillion won for HBM fab and packaging in Chungcheong; SK Hynix 20 trillion won for packaging at Cheongju</cite>—but 2029 timelines mean no near-term relief.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix, Samsung recover sharply after July 3 tech rout; SK Hynix +10.88%, Samsung +8.22%
news_pulse.implication: Thursday sell-off characterized as overreaction to Meta capacity-sharing headlines. Structural HBM demand intact. SK Hynix announced $29.4bn follow-on offering and Nasdaq ADR listing—dilution risk but expands capital access.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix unveils 100 trillion won investment: 80tn for M17 NAND fab (2029 start), 20tn for P&T7 packaging
news_pulse.implication: Addresses HBM server DRAM and enterprise SSD/NAND shortages. M17 operational 1H 2029. Confirms multi-year capex commitment; no near-term capacity relief but anchors long-term supply narrative.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026; capacity 120k–140k wpm
news_pulse.implication: Eases AI accelerator packaging bottleneck into 2027. Reduces stranded-die risk for Samsung/SK Hynix HBM output. Nvidia secures 60% of 2026 CoWoS; Samsung/AMD compete for remainder.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance ~$690bn (+81% YoY), with $700–900bn range per CreditSights
news_pulse.implication: 75% allocated to AI infra (GPUs, HBM servers). Wall Street consensus $930bn by 2028, $4.7tn 2025–2030. Sustains memory demand but raises monetization scrutiny and capex-fatigue risk.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q2 2026 contract pricing +58–63% QoQ (deceleration from Q1's +93–98%); NAND +70–75% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Rate-of-change decelerating but prices still rising. NAND now outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle. Spot buyer hesitation emerging June; not a top but plateau forming.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 8Gb spot hit $34.80 in early June (+3.57% WoW); DDR4 spot ($2.10/Gb) exceeds HBM3e contract ($1.70/Gb)
news_pulse.implication: Inverted value hierarchy reflects legacy scarcity. Buyers balking at chasing spot but contract allocations still tight. Supplier pricing power intact but demand elasticity appearing.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix pressing substrate suppliers for H2 2026 price cuts despite Super Cycle
news_pulse.implication: Margin management priority as raw-material costs stay high. Substrate makers warn of erosion. Signals pricing discipline ahead of potential cycle deceleration.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce April: Server DDR5 profitability overtook HBM in early 2026—historic first
news_pulse.implication: DDR5 ASP escalation so rapid it exceeded HBM margins. CSP long-term contracts lock price floors into 2027. Shifts incentive calculus for capacity allocation; could moderate HBM-only narrative.

brief.derivatives_signal: No KOSPI 200 futures or options data in payload. ADR proxies (SSNLF, HXSCL) OTC only—limited liquidity. Friday's 10.88%/8.22% rally following Thursday circuit-breaker suggests gamma/vol unwind complete. Watch July 7 Samsung prelim earnings for next volatility catalyst. Implied downside protection expensive post-selloff; consider cash-secured puts if thesis is long memory cycle.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung Q2 prelim earnings (July 7)—any miss on memory ASP or margin guides retest of Thursday lows
Hyperscaler July earnings guidance (MSFT 7/26, GOOGL 7/27, AMZN 7/31)—capex commentary and demand signals
TrendForce Q3 2026 DRAM/NAND contract forecast (due mid-July)—confirms deceleration vs plateau vs re-acceleration
SK Hynix $29.4bn follow-on pricing and allocation—dilution absorption test
CoWoS capacity data from TSMC July 18 earnings—confirms 120k+ wpm trajectory and 2027 easing thesis
